definitionBean.title: Heights and Distances
definitionBean.definition: Using trigonometric ratios to find the height of an object or the distance between two objects, using angles of elevation and depression.
definitionBean.explanation: angle of elevation is the angle formed when viewing an object above the horizontal line, while the angle of depression is formed when viewing an object below the horizontal line. Using these angles and the known distance/height trigonometric ratio are used to find the unknown value.
importantPoints: angle of elevation: angle formed when looking upward
angle of depression: angle formed when looking downward
Form a right-angled triangle and apply the appropriate trigonometric ratio
The angle of elevation and angle of depression are equal when they are alternate angles

realLifeExamples.title: Measuring the height of a tower
realLifeExamples.example: The height of a tower is found by standing at a known distance from its base and measuring the angle of elevation.

realLifeExamples.title: Distance from a ship to the shore
realLifeExamples.example: The distance is found by measuring the angle of depression of an object on the shore from the deck of a ship.

realLifeExamples.title: Height of an airplane
realLifeExamples.example: The flight altitude of an airplane is estimated by measuring its angle of elevation from the ground.

parts.statement: The shadow of a tree is 15 m long. If the angle of elevation of the sun is 45°, find the height of the tree.
parts.explanation: Given:nShadow of the tree = 15 mnangle of elevation = 45°nnLet Height of the tree = hnnIn the right-angled triangle,nntan 45° = h / 15nn1 = h / 15nnh = 15 mnnTherefore, Height of the tree = 15 m.

parts.statement: A person moving toward the base of a tower observes angles of elevation of 30° and 60° from two positions A and B, respectively. If the distance between A and B is 40 m, find the height of the tower.
parts.explanation: Let the height of the tower = h mnnLet the distance of the tower from B = x mnTherefore, distance from A = (x + 40) mnnB at:n tan60° = h/xn √3 = h/xn h = x√3nnA at:n tan30° = h/(x+40)n 1/√3 = h/(x+40)nnh = (x+40)/√3nnBoth expressions for h are equal:nnx√3 = (x+40)/√3nn3x = x + 40nn2x = 40nnx = 20 mnnTherefore, h = 20√3 mnn≈ 34.64 mnnTherefore, the height of the tower = 20√3 m (approximately 34.64 m).

parts.statement: An airplane is flying at an altitude of 3000 m above the ground. Its angle of elevation for a person on the ground is 30°. Find the horizontal distance between the person and the point directly below the airplane.
